## Data Acquisition Challenges
Utilizing a variety of physiological sensing modalities has several practical challenges that must be overcome to facilitate analysis for time-series data.

:::{.fragment .fade-left}
- Software Dependencies
    - Various sensor libraries provided by vendors require different operating systems, programming languages, and processor architecture (32 vs 64 bit)
:::

:::{.fragment .fade-left}
- Storage
    - High frequency data from various sources should be stored in a common database in a common format
    - Due to time-series nature of the data, synchronization is paramount to a high quality analysis
:::


:::{.fragment .fade-left}
- Scalability
    - Physiological data collection in an ecological setting may require different sensors for different tasks and may even need to consider multiple operators
:::

## Current Software Architecture

To overcome these challenges, a novel data acquisition system was developed utilizing open source tools and a distributed architecture.


::: {.column}
<div class="fragment" data-fragment-index="1">
  - <span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="2">Top layer uses a single control application to take in user input for testing configuration (which sensors, participant id#, etc.)</span>
  - <span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="3">Listeners receive configuration and manage sensor processes</span>
  - <span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="4">Sensors utilize MQTT Broker to route data to appropriate subscribers</span>
  - <span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="5">Subscribers include:</span>
    - <span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="6">Common time-series database (InfluxDB)</span>
    - <span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="7">Web based visualizations for real time dashboards (Grafana)</span>
    - <span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="8">Real time processing applications (Statistical models)</span>
</div>
:::
